thought.text: Excellent — the Vite dev server compiles the frontend TypeScript on-demand (both `@vite/client` and `entrypoints/desktop.ts` return HTTP 200 with compiled JS). Let me confirm a deeper module also compiles and do a final process/service check.

reasoning_content:
Both Vite's client and the desktop entry point compiled successfully (HTTP 200). The Vite dev server is working and can compile TypeScript on-demand. This confirms that the frontend asset pipeline (vite + dartsass) is operational, which was the "can take several minutes" step noted in the guide.

Just to be safe, I'll check whether the deeper app modules also get compiled, and also do a final summary check of all the processes.

Actually, I already have strong enough evidence. I'll check a few more modules to confirm that deep compilation works, and then wrap up.

action.command:
docker exec zammad-devcontainer-devcontainer-1 bash -c '
echo "=== deeper module: apps/desktop/main.ts ==="
curl -s -o /tmp/main.ts -w "HTTP %{http_code} size %{size_download}\n" --max-time 120 "http://127.0.0.1:3000/assets/frontend/vite-dev/apps/desktop/main.ts"
head -c 250 /tmp/main.ts; echo
echo ""
echo "=== fonts.css (frontend asset) ==="
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" --max-time 60 "http://127.0.0.1:3000/assets/frontend/fonts.css"
' 2>&1
